author: Jenny
text: Teachers…I’m a little confused. I see people asking for big Christmas gifts for their students like $20 Squishmallows, books, Lego sets, etc. Do you really spend $20 - $30 a student for Christmas? (Or ask donors to?) That seems like so much to me! Is that normal?

topReplies.author: Kara
topReplies.text: I think it’s nice to gift them something small. I’m doing a little build your own clay snowman and a copy of frosty after we read it as a class. The total was around $4 a student and they’re happy as can be!

topReplies.author: Katie (Mrs. B 🐝)
topReplies.text: I ordered this! And it had a $3 coupon 🙌☃️ & am doing individual hot chocolates too.

topReplies.author: Jenny
topReplies.text: Those are adorable! I love that!

topReplies.author: Shauna A
topReplies.text: That is odd. My students each get a coloring book and some kind of candy from dollar tree lol. That’s all I can do with 18 students every year.

topReplies.author: Jenny
topReplies.text: And that is perfect! I’m sure the kids loved them too!

topReplies.author: Jamie Ramos
topReplies.text: Honestly, I don’t do anything like that for my students. I’m starting to wonder if I’m a bad teacher…. 🤣

topReplies.author: Jenny
topReplies.text: Ummmm no! Not your responsibility to get each student $40-$50 worth of items

topReplies.author: Lori Tecler
topReplies.text: When I taught kindergarten I went to the home improvement store and bought a piece of shower board and had it cut into smaller pieces to make individual whiteboards for each student. Wrapped it up and added a dry erase marker. Not expensive and practical too.
